paper_title: Probing axions with neutron star inspirals and other stellar processes
notes: Theory/proposal paper (Hook & Huang 2017). Considers a tuned QCD axion (lighter by sqrt(epsilon), eq. 1.4) that can be sourced by dense objects and mediate forces between neutron stars. The headline result is a PROJECTION: future Advanced LIGO observations of neutron star inspirals/mergers 'can probe many orders of magnitude of axion parameter space' (abstract; Fig 6 caption: 'region ... can potentially be tested with future LIGO measurements of neutron star mergers'). The parameter plane in Fig 6 is Log10[GeV/F_a] (i.e. 1/f_a in GeV^-1) vs Log10[m_a/eV]. The exclusion regions shown in Fig 6 (Earth, Sun, SN1987A, superradiance, pulsar, BBN) are reinterpretations of other experiments'/observations' data (neutron eDM measurements, pion masses, Borexino solar neutrinos, Hulse-Taylor/PSR J0737-3039 orbital decay, superradiance) applied to this specific non-standard axion model, presented as context rather than a headline new measured limit derived by the paper. No new experimental exclusion curve of the paper's own is presented as the main result; the main result is a forecast for LIGO. Reported as projection with no points.
